This suggests that the current penalty setup may be too advantageous, violating principles of game balance. The authors propose a reconfiguration grounded in expected goals modeling, which uses generalized additive models with beta distribution and logit link to predict goal probabilities based on distance, angle, and defender proximity. The model's objective is to maintain the same expected goal value (~75%) but adjust the physical parameters of the kick—distance and angle—to achieve fairness. The failure mode occurs when the model underestimates or overestimates these factors, leading to misalignment between perceived difficulty and actual outcome. Dualities emerge in how spatial configuration affects both offensive strategy and defensive positioning. The derivation hinges on empirical validation of shot data from 2018 World Cup, ensuring that adjustments reflect real-world performance rather than theoretical constructs.
